# `sesam reveal` used to overwrite any plaintext that differed from its object -
# unsealed edits included, silently. Now it tells an edit from a stale copy: a
# plaintext that is the decryption of no object version was written here, and
# only naming it or --all takes it away.

sesam-repo admin base.txt edit.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt db.txt
exec sesam add db.txt --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add db'

# An edit that was never sealed.
cp $TMPDIR/edit.txt db.txt
exec sesam status
stdout 'M db.txt'
stdout '1 modified'

# A plain reveal keeps it and says so.
exec sesam reveal
stderr 'kept 1 edited secret \(not revealed\)'
stderr 'sesam:   db.txt'
stderr 'sesam seal. keeps your version'
stderr 'sesam reveal <path>. takes the object'
exec cat db.txt
stdout 'MY UNSAVED WORK'

# A plain clean keeps it too.
exec sesam clean
stderr 'kept 1 edited or unsealed secret'
exists db.txt

# Forcing either one takes it away: clean deletes, reveal restores the object.
exec sesam clean --unsealed
! exists db.txt
exec sesam reveal
exec cat db.txt
stdout 'ORIGINAL'

cp $TMPDIR/edit.txt db.txt
exec sesam reveal --all
! stderr 'kept'
exec cat db.txt
stdout 'ORIGINAL'

# Naming a path takes the object for it alone and names the edit it threw away.
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt other.txt
exec sesam add other.txt --group admin
cp $TMPDIR/edit.txt db.txt
cp $TMPDIR/edit.txt other.txt
exec sesam reveal db.txt
stderr 'discarded your unsealed edits in 1 secret'
stderr 'sesam:   db.txt'
stderr 'kept 1 edited secret'
stderr 'sesam:   other.txt'
exec cat db.txt
stdout 'ORIGINAL'
exec cat other.txt
stdout 'MY UNSAVED WORK'

# Paths a reveal cannot write are refused, not ignored.
! exec sesam reveal nope.txt
stderr 'nope.txt: not a tracked secret'
! exec sesam reveal --all db.txt
stderr 'it takes no paths'

-- base.txt --
ORIGINAL
-- edit.txt --
MY UNSAVED WORK
